prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry: thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand rules, border states, CTT tolerance, swap precedence/equity/customs eligibility/min notification/prohibited trades. Modes (ADM declares): Normal; Adverse Weather(shorter sweeps); Capacity Reduction State(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery Phase(RFM exits; preserves operator logic); Contingency Fallback(Contingency Operations Console); Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms). Actors: RFM=Regional Flow Manager(resolves swap disputes); Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison; Tower Supervisor(stand readiness; may reject unsafe swaps); ADM=Airport Duty Manager(Medical Diversion Notice, Customs Hold Release Note; checks Apron Sweep Completion Note vs swaps); Ramp Control Lead(Apron Sweep Completion Note; checks swaps on Ramp Movement Board); Ground Handling Dispatcher(Towbar Shortage Report; updates Handling Resource Planner); Aircraft Operator Rep(Crew Duty Extension Log; records swap concurrence in Foxglove); Airline Operations Coordinator(revised TOBT; uses release note for customs eligibility; enters swap); Slot Coordinator(reviews Blueharbor exceptions; sends Slot Swap Permission Email after recorded governance checks); NOL=Network Operations Liaison(monitors swap displacement); Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator; MBO=Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward. Parts: Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform; Airline Interface Adapter; Sector Load Monitor; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service; CAM=Capacity Assessment Module(AAR; Arrival Regulation Console; Tactical Regulation Proposal); Weather Ingest Gateway; Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; GDP; Pushback Window Token; evaluates swaps); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(TOBT=Target Off Block Time; Collaborative Decision Log: flights, reason, confirmations, governance outcome, decision time; Identity Access Service; holds swap pending and blocks Blueharbor publish if customs incomplete); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager; suppresses if stand not ready; recalculates after swap, prevents fix peaks); Gate Conflict Detector; Audit Event Ledger(readiness, releases, approvals/rejections/cancellations/overrides); Flight Data Exchange(Flight Intent Message after final swap); Common Situation Display(CTT/TOBT); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Alert Distribution

New part:
S688: The System Support Engineer investigates technical failures in submission, validation, or publication without altering the operational decision unless authorized through the defined control process.
S689: The Post Operations Report includes swap volume, rejection reasons, approval latency, compliance with revised times, and any equity concerns identified during the operating period.
S690: Aerodrome infrastructure events are treated as capacity inputs when they affect runway availability, taxi route usability, stand access, lighting performance, or supporting navigation services.
S691: The Regional Flow Platform records each event as an operational constraint with an effective time, expected duration, affected resource, confidence level, and approving authority.
S692: The Airport Duty Manager is responsible for ensuring that declared service reductions are entered promptly and that the operational description is consistent with local aerodrome control procedures.
S693: The Tower Supervisor uses the Runway Lighting Outage Card to confirm which runway lighting elements are unavailable before approving the operational status shown in the Tower Sequence Manager.
S694: When lighting performance limits night or low-visibility operations, the Capacity Assessment Module converts the limit into a runway configuration constraint rather than treating it as a general advisory.
S695: The Airport CDM Portal presents infrastructure events to authorized airport, airline, and flow management users as part of the shared operating picture.
S696: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the published constraint when it changes the usable runway rate, taxi-out predictability, or the feasibility of the active demand plan.
S697: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates the operational effect by comparing the affected resource with the current Airport Capacity Plan and the active weather state.
S698: If the event reduces arrival throughput, the Arrival Regulation Console applies the revised Airport Acceptance Rate after confirmation by the Regional Flow Manager.
S699: If the event reduces departure throughput, the Departure Metering Service updates metering rates and provides revised inputs to the Slot Allocation Engine.
S700: The Slot Allocation Engine uses the reduced capacity value to protect fairness while avoiding schedules that exceed the declared infrastructure capability.
S701: The Demand Prediction Service recalculates short-term demand against the constrained capacity so that delay and queue forecasts reflect the published limitation.
S702: The Tower Sequence Manager displays the accepted constraint to support runway sequencing decisions and to reduce conflicting tactical instructions.
S703: The Ramp Movement Board receives the same operational status so that apron movements can be coordinated with restricted taxi routes or stand access limitations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
